claim_boundary: C016 records a decisive elementary obstruction to positive-only anti-checkers against arbitrary circuits. H112 and H113 are terminal; H116 is a repaired open route.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: a positive-only list may fail to catch circuits whose accepted language is a strict superset of SAT
attacks.method: Take the constant circuit C_top(x)=1. It has constant size and accepts every satisfiable formula in every produced list, so it has no false negative on the list although it is not a SAT decider.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: a range-avoidance decoder may be unable to force a false negative for every candidate SAT circuit
attacks.method: Apply the claimed decoder to C_top(x)=1. No satisfiable formula F can satisfy C_top(F)=0, so the required decoded output does not exist.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: the repaired route may still admit C_top
attacks.method: Require global SAT soundness C(G)=1 implies G is satisfiable. C_top violates the promise whenever an unsatisfiable encoding exists.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: a small sound circuit may accept every listed positive example by recognizing the list
attacks.method: Charge the total encoded list size and compare it with n^k. A membership circuit for the finite list is sound because every listed formula has a witness; the construction must make every such membership circuit exceed the target size.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: the constructor may secretly decide whether each candidate circuit is SAT-sound
attacks.method: Treat soundness only as a semantic quantifier restriction. The algorithm receives 1^n, not a circuit and not a soundness certificate.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: a lower bound only for sound incomplete circuits may fail to rule out exact SAT circuits
attacks.method: Any exact SAT circuit is sound. Therefore a list hitting every size-n^k sound circuit also hits every exact SAT circuit of that size.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: dropping negative examples from the two-sided anti-checker may preserve the original consequence
attacks.method: The all-accepting circuit proves that arbitrary-circuit anti-checkers need either negative labeled examples, a soundness promise, or an independently proved soundness-enforcing normalization.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: range avoidance alone may select the desired SAT error polarity
attacks.method: The constant-one circuit has only false-positive SAT errors. Any universal reduction must either allow that polarity or impose and preserve a soundness promise.
